summary:
What changes. One run option, --planning-review stage|none, recorded in state.md for the whole run like backchain_passes; a saved 1.21.x run is refused, nothing is migrated. stage is today, and its packets stay byte-identical. none starts no Improve review after spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan or test-spec; the system-test-author, release-plan and end-of-work reviews stay. Your candidate once (one merged review at plan) is specified but not built: even free it leaves at least 36.5 of Grok medium's 72.7 minutes, it is the largest increment, and its design has open problems.

Minutes. Review is 54% (Luna xhigh) and 58% (Grok medium) of the planning window [M]. Grok medium: none leaves 26.8 to 30.3 of 72.7 if no work moves into authoring, up to about 44 if first-pass review work does (unmeasured). Luna xhigh: 172.5 of 375.9 at best; no review change reaches 30 there.

Quality. Nothing looks a second time at planning. Review caught five warranted fixes on Luna, 10 of 15 real plan-stage platform errors once the claim bullet was added (Sonnet, condensed packets), and a missing importable-server seam on a Sonnet battleship run: the defect class that cost Luna 165.9 minutes of redo when review missed it. The escape rate without review is unknown.

What carries the exit criterion. ShipLoop's gates at complete; a new test-author probe that runs the focused commands and refuses tests that cannot load; the later red, green and regression gates. Whether spec criteria are complete and oracles independent has no script-run check in any mode. The carve-out says so; it strains your steps-iterate-until-confirmed and enterprise-rigour rules.

Order and default. Probe, SPEC carve-out, option, none. The default stays stage until a Grok medium none probe (twice) and a post-hoc review of its documents are read; the flip is then its own SPEC commit plus one constant.
option: Name planning_review. CLI flag --planning-review {stage,none} on init and on workspace start (workspace start forwards it to init, as --backchain-passes is forwarded). Values: stage (today: one Improve child after each of spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec) and none (no child at those five). A third value, once, is specified under modes but is registered only if the owner chooses it (decision D2): each increment adds its value to PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES together with its behaviour, so no commit records a value the engine ignores (I1 registers stage only; the draft's I1 recorded once and none while executing stage, which an attack rightly called an option that lies). Default: stage in code through I4. Recommended default after the measurement gate: none, flipped only by I5 (its own dated SPEC commit stating the default and the measured basis, then one constant, DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW in shiploop_stage_spec.py, re-exported by shiploop_navigator.py). State key planning_review in _STATE_KEYS, written by new_state(planning_review=...), validated in new_state ('planning review must be one of ...') and in _validate_current_state, read through recorded_planning_review(state). Retry guard: one shared helper _require_retry_fixed_option(existing, requested, run_dir, flag, label, recorded) in shiploop_protocol.py (S-12: a third copy of the lint and backchain guards is not added); _require_retry_backchain_passes is rewritten onto it with byte-identical messages so its tests stay green, and _require_retry_planning_review is its second caller at both retry sites (init and workspace start): a retry naming another value is refused, naming the recorded value, the fresh --run-dir route and 'only the owner starts a fresh run'. No --set verb and no environment variable (a new surface, S-13). Old runs: a saved state without the key is refused by the existing generic missing-fields check with FRESH_RUN_HINT; I ran the analogous check on an unchanged scratch export and it prints 'navigator state has unsupported or missing fields (missing: backchain_passes); a run saved by an older ShipLoop cannot be loaded. Preserve it; this ShipLoop cannot resume it. Start new work with init or workspace start in a fresh --run-dir.' [M]. Nothing is migrated or shimmed. The name stays stage|none because stage_spec.PHASES already means prelude, inner and outer. The option covers five stages, not the seven of guidance.PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES (system-test-author and release-plan too), which stays static because it feeds STEP_PLANNING_STAGES [M, shiploop_navigator.py]. guidance.prompt takes planning_review keyword-only with the literal default 'stage' (like backchain_passes, a89135f7), so the PROMPTS catalog and its test are untouched by the later default flip, and navigator.render passes the recorded mode.

modes.semantics: Today's behaviour, schedule and text. Every result at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan and test-spec parks the action and starts its own Improve child. Packets are byte-identical to the current tree in every increment (accepted attack findings A1-4 and A2-9: the draft reworded the shared Improve sentences for every mode, which would have changed the revert target and confounded any stage-versus-none comparison). It is the control cell and the revert target.
modes.schedule: Two-item run: spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan W1, test-spec W1, step-plan W2, test-spec W2, carry-forward (last item), system-test-author, release-plan = 10 children, five in the planning window (intake to the first test-spec accept) [M, the draft's scratch walk of the pure navigator, reproduced by the attack]. Each starts when the producer's result is accepted into active_improve and reviews that stage's documents (shiploop_knowledge_home.STAGE_FILES: spec -> living spec.md and the feature spec.md; test-strategy -> test-strategy.md; plan -> the feature plan.md and README.md; step-plan -> the feature plan.md; test-spec -> the feature test-spec.md).
modes.packet_text: Unchanged. Improve line: 'Improve: Every <stage> result, including blocked and repeat, starts this action's Improve child. If work cannot continue, submit outcome blocked with a truthful summary; when the run stops blocked, the next packet prints its Resume command.' COMMON, the plan, step-plan and test-spec duties, the plan purpose line and the test-facility sentence keep today's wording, because they are swapped only for a stage that starts no child in the recorded mode. Verified by golden: every planning-stage packet and the plan Improve packet, both delegations, equal the text captured before I2 (the 20-of-20 method of a34a6ee6).
modes.expected_minutes: Measured, not expected [M, stage-clock.md, grok-medium-improve-children.json, run-doc files]. Grok medium (grok-4.7, 1.21.0): planning window 72.7 min; Improve children 42.4 min on the children clock (start.json to receipt; 58%; spec 15.2, test-strategy 13.1, plan 5.2, step-plan 6.4, test-spec 2.5; 26 passes) and 45.88 on the exporter clock (producer accept to improve-complete). Luna xhigh: window 375.9; children 203.4 (54%; spec 44.5, test-strategy 61.1, plan 56.9, step-plan 26.7, test-spec 14.2; 22 passes). One run each; stage times vary about 2x between runs of the same model.

modes.semantics: No model-run Improve child at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan or test-spec. Each result is accepted on ShipLoop's own checks at complete and the graph advances directly, as at intake or prepare. The system-test-author, release-plan and last carry-forward children keep running. Consequences stated in the SPEC carve-out: the plan child's improve-reconcile route and the plan-time experiments it hosts do not exist (nothing dangles: the route is printed only in the child packet [M]); the plan's assumption list is still checked at complete by _check_submitted_assumptions [M]; spec and test-strategy are committed to docs/shiploop at their own accept, before any review, so later runs inherit an unreviewed spec [M, knowledge_home.commit follows any accepted stage that changed the home]; the first Improve child of a run, and the first resolution of the Improve card (done at improve-bind, not at init [M, standalone.resolve_skill]), moves to the end of the run, so a missing card first shows after all implementation work (a stall with the action pending, recoverable; a known limit, no engine change). none with --backchain-passes none leaves no model-run second look at the plan graph: document it as the highest-risk combination, do not refuse it (KISS, as 2026-10-04 did not refuse backchain none).
modes.schedule: Two-item run: carry-forward (last item), system-test-author, release-plan = 3 children, none in the planning window [M, scratch walk]. Nothing reviews the five planning documents at planning time. Schedule logic: reviewed_stages('none') = with_improve('always') minus {spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec}, i.e. {system-test-author, release-plan}, plus the unchanged carry-forward rule.
modes.packet_text: At each of the five stages the Improve line reads: 'Improve: no Improve child starts after this result in this run (planning_review: none); ShipLoop's own checks at complete are the only gate before the graph advances. If work cannot continue, submit outcome blocked with a truthful summary; when the run stops blocked, the next packet prints its Resume command.' (trimmed per accepted finding A1-8: the draft's extra 'confirm each Done-when' sentence repeated text every mode already prints). Swaps made only for a stage that starts no child, from one table with an import-time guard: COMMON 'Only planning results (...) get an actual Improve-skill handoff' becomes the list of stages that do in this mode; the plan duty paragraph becomes 'After creating the initial steps, submit this producer result; ShipLoop's own checks at complete are its gate, and the accepted plan is what dependent work builds on. Link the created plan and any execution graph in evidence_refs. Do not schedule a review stage or claim one ran.'; the step-plan duty sentence (delegated and inline variants) becomes 'ShipLoop's checks at complete are the gate for the created steps and graph; no Improve child reviews them in this run.'; the test-spec duty becomes 'No Improve child reviews this result in this run. Do not schedule a review stage or claim one ran.'; the plan purpose line drops 'its Improve child evaluates whether the evidence supports it'; the test-facility sentence drops 'and the Improve child's context/notes'; the 'Planning experiments guide' and 'Planning investigation notebook' lines are not printed (they belong to the plan child). Sentences that name Improve without promising a child ('Do not embed an Improve review campaign in this result', the status and narrative lines, 'the next Improve packet can recover them') stay, in a reasoned allowlist the scan test reads.
modes.expected_minutes: Grok medium, window 72.7: 30.3 on the children clock (72.7 minus 42.4) or 26.8 on the exporter clock (72.7 minus 45.88) if no work moves into authoring [M arithmetic]; the five first passes took 13.3 min [M, file mtimes: spec 4.7, test-strategy 2.2, plan 1.4, step-plan 4.3, test-spec 0.7], so if all first-pass review work moves into the producers the window is about 40 to 44 (the share that moves is unmeasured). Narrow window (intake to plan accept, 57.8): 24.3 or 21.6, up to 32.6 if the three global first passes (8.3) move. Luna xhigh, window 375.9: 172.5 at best (narrow window 279.9: 117.4); worst case about 247 if all 74.4 min of pass-1 time moved [M for 74.4, ledger F4; the share is unmeasured]; the ledger's floor with no model-run Improve and no Backchain loop beyond the draft is 115-131 [I], so no review value reaches 30 on Luna xhigh and the rest needs other levers (L11 script lint 35-55, L13 backchain none 22-57, effort) outside this change. Sonnet 5.5: its five battleship planning children took 13 passes in 125 s [M, ledger], about 2 min saved of a 4.7 min window, against one measured catch (commit b1e196d).

modes.semantics: CONDITIONAL, not built unless the owner chooses it (D2); your candidate, refined. One review of the run's global planning documents: spec and test-strategy results advance without a child; the plan result starts one child (the existing plan child: same bound runtime, same two-review or unchanged-first-pass exit, no cap, reconcile and plan-time experiments kept) over the accepted spec, test-strategy and plan together; step-plan and test-spec keep their own per-item children (the per-item merge is rejected: _canonical_result allows steps, test_commands, criteria and paths only on a done step-plan result, so a child bound to test-spec could only revise and re-author [M]). Script-owned: the covered stages' done-when criteria added to the plan child's frozen exit (+564 B on the 9,216 B contract budget: spec 310, test-strategy 254 [M, measured with stage_exit]); the covered documents prepended to the child's scope from STAGE_FILES; the covered-results block printed from state; the Improve prompt and references composed from covered stages; one generic cross-document clause added to the planning review focus for once only. Two design faults the attacks found, fixed in this specification: (1) the child's frozen repeat clause says a finding that invalidates an accepted spec or test-strategy premise means 'report cancelled' [M, improve_start_contract], which collides with repairing a covered document in place; for once it is reworded so a defect the child can repair together with the dependent documents is fixed in place and only a premise it cannot repair takes the cancelled/improve-reconcile route (a test on the frozen text); (2) the plan child prints no improve-commit route today [M, _render_improve planning_reconcile branch], so a child editing three knowledge-home documents would commit by raw git (counted as model glue, S-4/S-5); for once it prints the improve-commit lines (one conditional). A covered stage's accepted record cannot be amended (the child's final_result is canonicalised as plan): a changed decision is made in the files, committed, named in evidence_refs and stated in the summary.
modes.schedule: Two-item run: plan (covering spec, test-strategy, plan), step-plan W1, test-spec W1, step-plan W2, test-spec W2, carry-forward, system-test-author, release-plan = 8 children, three in the planning window [M, scratch walk]. The plan child starts when the plan result is accepted, the last point before prepare, so improve-reconcile (legal only at the bound plan child before prepare [M]) keeps its route; after a reconcile restart at spec once starts one child, stage three.
modes.packet_text: spec and test-strategy: 'Improve: no Improve child starts after this result; the Improve child that starts at plan reviews it together with the other planning results. If work cannot continue, submit outcome blocked ...'. plan: 'Improve: Every plan result, including blocked and repeat, starts this action's Improve child. It is this run's one review of the planning documents: it also covers the accepted spec and test-strategy results, which ShipLoop lists in its packet.' Plus a block ShipLoop writes into the plan child's packet: 'This child also covers these accepted results, which advanced without their own review; ShipLoop froze their documents into this child's scope and their done-when criteria into its exit condition. Review the three results together and against each other: a criterion with no check, a check that needs a file, module or fixture that no step or earlier work creates, two statements that contradict. A covered result's accepted record cannot be amended: change a decision in the files, commit it, name the revised files in evidence_refs and state the change in this result's summary.' step-plan, test-spec and every other stage: unchanged.
modes.expected_minutes: Unknown; no such run exists. Window 72.7 on Grok medium: at least 39.2 on the children clock or 36.5 on the exporter clock even if the merged child cost nothing (33.5 or 36.16 removed), so once cannot reach 30 on the owner's window (intake to the first test-spec accept [M, journal 'Planning time']); the three separate first passes alone took 8.3 min [M mtimes], so a merged child is more likely 8 to 15 than free [I]. On the narrow window (to plan accept, 57.8) it is 24.3 or 21.6 plus the merged child, under 30 only if the merged child costs under 5.7 or 8.4 min. Luna xhigh: at least 213.4 (375.9 minus 162.5) and at most 375.9; ledger lever L3 (a related one-review-at-the-end shape) estimated 118-178 min saved [I].

engine_changes:
All symbols read in the source tree d1cca62f (ShipLoop 0.53.1) [M]. Verified this round on a scratch export of the tree, read-only: the generic missing-key refusal; the real planning-packet inventory (stage-mode packets have 11, 12, 20, 12 and 11 sentences naming Improve at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan and test-spec); the probe judge on seven recorded outputs, draft against fixed; per-pass minutes of the Grok run by file mtime; the schedule logic and the suite failures at a none default come from the draft's scratch prototype and the attack's logs (re-summed: 177 added failures in 17 of 22 schedule-sensitive suites). I did not rebuild a prototype of the revised design. Increment order: I3, I0, I1, I2, [I4 if D2], I5.

I3, test-author probe. shiploop_stage_spec.py: 'test-probe' in COMPLETE_RUNS; complete_runs=('test-probe',) on the test-author row (revise is already an outcome of every INNER row from test-spec on, so _remedy('test-author') is revise [M, _finish]). shiploop_test_loop.py: PROBE_STAGE, = stage_spec.with_complete_run('test-probe'); stage_commands runs focused commands only for PROBE_STAGE (add it beside test-green and RED_STAGE); verify: probe = stage == PROBE_STAGE and judge(row, code, output, red=red or (probe and code != 0)), so exit 0 is judged in passing mode (a counted test, every listed ID shown) and a non-zero exit in red mode (a failing test inside a test); good = ('red', 'passed') for the probe; its own header ('did not run a test') and closing sentence naming the placeholder rule in place of 'did not fail as expected' and 'Fix the tests or their setup (not the product code)', which the red branch would print; record['expect'] = 'a test ran'; _explain adds the placeholder sentence for no-tests, too-few-tests, ids-missing, uncounted and not-red at the probe. shiploop_navigator.py: _test_red_gate becomes one focused-run gate taking the stage (S-12), called for RED_STAGE and PROBE_STAGE from the dispatch complete branch; done results only; red_na applies at RED only. shiploop_prompts.py: one generic sentence in the test-author duty and one in the step-plan duty (S-8, no language wording). Why the draft's red-mode probe was wrong: in red mode judge() returns 'green' for any exit 0 unless a count says ran == 0, so an exit-0 run with no readable count, or with listed IDs never shown, was accepted [M, shiploop_test_loop.judge]; reproduced on seven recorded outputs.

I1, option plumbing, value stage only. shiploop_stage_spec.py: PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES = ('stage',), DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW = 'stage', reviewed_stages(mode) = with_improve('always') for stage. shiploop_navigator.py: 'planning_review' in _STATE_KEYS; new_state(..., planning_review=DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW) with a _need on the value; _validate_current_state _need ('unsupported planning review option; expected one of ...'); recorded_planning_review(state) and its __all__ entry; re-exports; render passes the recorded mode to guidance.prompt. shiploop_protocol.py: --planning-review choices=navigator.PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES on the workspace-start and init parsers; passthrough; the shared retry helper at both retry sites; planning_review=args.planning_review or DEFAULT in the new_state call. shiploop_prompts.py: prompt and duty take keyword-only planning_review (default the literal 'stage', validated), no text change. shiploop_navigator_dry_run.py: run_scenario(..., planning_review=) and graph-dry-run --planning-review. Saved runs: no code.

I2, none. shiploop_stage_spec.py: PLANNING_CHOICE_STAGES = {spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec}; PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES = ('stage', 'none'); reviewed_stages('none') = with_improve('always') minus PLANNING_CHOICE_STAGES. Do not redefine guidance.PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES (the seven): it feeds STEP_PLANNING_STAGES, which drives which packets print accepted spec and plan sources [M]. Leave _IMPROVE_STAGES static (KISS: a record at an unreviewed stage can only come from a hand edit; the required set and the active-child check carry the rule). shiploop_navigator.py: _improve_checkpoint replaces 'stage in guidance.PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES' with 'stage in stage_spec.reviewed_stages(recorded_planning_review(state))' (the only place that decides whether a result parks a child; called by apply and by _validate_current_state); _validate_current_state builds the required set 'planning' from reviewed_stages(mode), keeping the no-test-item exclusion (item_scope.no_test_item), and rewords two refusals ('... including every planning-stage result this run's planning_review option reviews'; 'a stage that does not start an Improve child in this run (planning_review: X)'); _improve_line(state, stage); the 'Planning phase intent' block and the plan purpose line and the two plan-child lines depend on 'plan' in reviewed_stages(mode). shiploop_prompts.py: prompt and duty take the mode; one swap table of (stage, old sentence, new sentence) pairs applied only for a planning stage that starts no child, with an import-time check that each old sentence occurs exactly once (the _INLINE_DUTY_PARAGRAPHS pattern); the COMMON handoff sentence is built from the mode's reviewed list and equals today's literal for stage (tested); 'improves' for TEST_FACILITY_HANDOFF becomes 'this stage starts a child in this mode'. Stage-mode text is byte-identical. shiploop_navigator_dry_run.py: REVIEWED3 and activity() become a per-mode literal table (an independent oracle on purpose). skills/shiploop-e2e-audit/harness/dag_replay.py (the literal _PLANNING_CHECKPOINTS and _path_steps, and synthetic cases that finish a child at spec, test-strategy or step-plan) takes the case's mode; workflow_review.py (imports that literal; marks 'accepted planning-stage result has no Improve record' unknown and not comparable) reads the recorded mode; both keep a literal second copy on purpose. Docs in the same commit (the 2f091a35 lesson: the tree must not tell the host two things).

I4, once (conditional). reviewed_stages('once'); stage_spec.covered_stages(stage, mode); improve_start_contract appends stage_exit for every covered stage and rewords the planning repeat clause for once; the script prepends the covered documents to context.scope; _render_improve prints the covered-results block from state and prints the improve-commit lines for the plan child under once; guidance._improve_prompt and the stage-reference printing take the covered stages; the once-only cross-document clause; _derived_improve_receipt summary names the covered stages; narrative wording; a SPEC amendment commit first (SPEC-first), then the value joins PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES with its behaviour.

I5, default flip: a docs-only SPEC commit stating the default and the measured basis, then DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW = 'none' with explicit planning_review='stage' in every fixture that walks the old schedule, in make_packet_frame.py, dag_replay.py cases and the regenerated references/graph-dry-run-scenario.json, in the same commit as the flip so main never has a red suite.

Unchanged: Stage.improve rows, guidance.PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES, finish_improve, shiploop_standalone_improve binding, _improve_change_gate and improve_changes, knowledge_home, shiploop_assumptions, the vendored Until Loop (test/improve.test.sh pins its hashes).

consumers.what: shiploop_navigator._validate_current_state (planning <= records <= expected and two refusal texts) and _improve_checkpoint
consumers.action: Make both mode-aware in I2 (required set from reviewed_stages(mode)); reword the two refusals so they do not say 'only planning stages and the final carry-forward do' in a run whose mode excludes a planning stage. Without this every none state is refused ('Improve results must belong to completed steps, including every planning-stage result') [M, code read; the draft's scratch prototype reproduced it].

consumers.what: Producer packet text that promises a handoff: _improve_line, COMMON, the plan duty, the step-plan duty (delegated and inline variants), the test-spec duty, the plan purpose line, the experiment locator lines, TEST_FACILITY_HANDOFF
consumers.action: Silent breakage: the host would be told two things. I2 swaps each sentence for a stage that starts no child, from one table with an import-time guard, and keeps stage-mode text byte-identical (golden). A test derives from the real render, for every mode, delegation and planning stage, that the Improve line says a child starts if and only if the stage is in reviewed_stages(mode) and that every other sentence naming Improve is allowlisted with a reason or absent. The draft's three-phrase scan missed 8 to 15 Improve sentences per none packet [M, attack, inventory re-run: 11, 12, 20, 12, 11 in stage mode].

consumers.what: Documents the host reads that state the schedule: skills/shiploop/SKILL.md ('When Improve runs', 'Experiment-informed planning', 'Test stages not applicable', the step-plan review sentence, flag summaries), README.md, commands/shiploop-complete.md, references navigator.md, state-files.md, graph-dry-run.md, planning-experiments.md, improve-context.md, research-loop.md, execution-planning.md, backchain-planning.md, parallel-chain.md, behavioral-requirements.md, testing-and-documentation.md, shiploop-e2e-audit MOCK-REPLAY.md
consumers.action: Update in the same commit as the packet text and add a document scan test in the style of BackchainGateDocumentsTest with a reasoned allowlist. parallel-chain.md's 'review required' sentences are host-verified text only: the script refuses a chain bind only while an Improve child is active [M]; under none a chain binds a graph that only the structural backchain-check has seen.

workflow_review marks an engine-valid none run not comparable without failing (silent); dag_replay fails shiploop-mock-replay, which runs on every push, once the default flips. Make both read the recorded mode with a literal table per mode, pin planning_review='stage' in existing cases until I5, add their own tests and a change note under changes/shiploop-e2e-audit/.

consumers.what: shiploop_navigator_dry_run, references/graph-dry-run-scenario.json and the schedule-walking suites
consumers.action: Only at the default flip (I5): 177 added failures in 17 of 22 schedule-sensitive suites on a scratch copy with the default flipped to none [M, attack logs re-summed: actual-improve-cli 23, callback-contract 6, consumer-delivery 30, delegation 13, guidance 13, improve-schedule 8, navigator-contract 21, navigator-dry-run 26 (aborts early, a lower bound), navigator-v4 10, packet-bounds 1, planning-context 2, quality 1, rehydration 5, revise 10, standalone-improve 2, v4-consumers 4, status-display 2]. The draft listed 9 test files. I5 pins planning_review='stage' where a helper finishes a child at spec, adds a none-default test and regenerates the scenario. With default stage (I1 to I4) the schedule-sensitive suites pass unchanged [I].

Not tolerant of none as the default: its loop 'while not (current_stage == plan and active_improve)' never meets a plan child and ends in NavigatorError 'navigator is not active' [M, code read; the attack saw it after 38 iterations]. Pin planning_review='stage' in I5 (the frame depicts a plan-stage Improve review). Because stage packets are byte-identical, the frame and its .source hash do not change at I2 or I4 (the draft expected a hand regeneration).

consumers.what: Saved runs and in-flight E2E runs recorded by 1.21.x (no planning_review key)
consumers.action: By design (one supported version): refused with FRESH_RUN_HINT, no migration. The two 1.21.0 run directories under /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261005 would be refused on resume; no E2E process was running when I looked [M, ps]. Tell the E2E session before the release lands (D8).

Handoff to the Run Review session, not edited here. Children are derived from improve/ directories, so zero children is tolerated. Facts it needs: (1) the run's recorded planning_review from state.md, as it records backchain_passes today; (2) _improve_totals({}) returns zero passes and zero minutes with no reason, so a run with no improve evidence and a none run look the same: unmeasured must be unknown, not zero; (3) the phase-1 expectation text 'The script accepts each only after its Improve review' is untrue under none; (4) baseline rows carry host, model and effort but not the mode, so cells must not be compared across modes silently [I].

consumers.what: E2E harness (test/shiploop_e2e/run.py, metrics.py) and its option channel
consumers.action: metrics counts directories under improve/ and defaults to 0; no verdict reads the count [M]. No change. The draft said E2E had no channel for a stage control cell; it does not need one: run.py's --source checkout builds this checkout [M, docstring], so control (stage) and treatment (the same checkout with DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW='none' as an uncommitted one-line edit, or the flag in the case prompt [I]) run from the same code. Narrow SPEC edit (c) of the draft is dropped: no harness code reads the mode except workflow_review.

consumers.what: Progress, status, narrative, report, context index, planning context, plan-dispatcher and chain code
consumers.action: They read improve_results through .get or test only active_improve; the 'Done: spec (reviewed by Improve)' status text is derived from improve_results and is correctly absent under none [M, navigator line that builds it]; the chain code refuses a bind only while a child is active [I].

commit follows any accepted stage that changed docs/shiploop, not fixed closes [M], so S-11 holds. Under none the spec and test-strategy are committed before any review; later runs inherit an unreviewed spec. Stated in the carve-out; a none-mode test asserts the spec is committed after the spec stage through the real CLI.

consumers.action: none removes the route: nothing dangles because it is printed only in the child packet [M]; stated in the carve-out, with qualifiers added to planning-experiments.md, improve-context.md and SKILL.md ('The existing Plan Improve child investigates consequential assumptions').

spec_carve_out:
Own commit (I0), after the probe commit I3 and before any option code, dated 2026-10-05, like 9747d769. Blocked until the owner answers D1, D2 and D3. Four SPEC edits and one test change.

Edit (a), S-10 head: 'Except for the carve-out below, there is no iteration cap' becomes 'Except for the carve-outs below, there is no iteration cap'. Edit (b), end of the 2026-10-04 carve-out: 'Quality, test and Improve loops are not covered; their no-cap rule stands.' becomes 'Quality and test loops are not covered, nor are Improve loops except as the next carve-out says; their no-cap rule stands.' Edit (c) of the draft (the 'S-9, S-10' table row 'read against the run's recorded planning_review') is dropped: no harness code except workflow_review reads the mode, so the sentence would be untrue. Edit (d), insert after the 2026-10-04 carve-out and before S-11 (it must come after: BackchainPassesOptionTest.test_the_spec_carve_out_names_the_option_the_code_defines splits at the first '**S-10 carve-out' and reads to '**S-11'; the new text names no --backchain-passes flag and no 'defaults to X pass' phrase, checked against both regexes [M]):

**S-10 carve-out, owner decision 2026-10-05** (anchor: the owner's rule that
planning takes no more than 30 minutes, decided after the evaluation of the
skill-craft 1.21.0 battleship runs on Luna xhigh and Grok medium, not a clause
this serves; it relaxes S-9, S-10 and the rule that a step iterates until a
check confirms each exit criterion, for the Improve review of planning results,
and says so). The run option `planning_review` (state option `planning_review`,
recorded in `state.md` at `init` or `workspace start`, never changed afterwards;
a saved run without it is refused) selects which of the five planning results
`spec`, `test-strategy`, `plan`, `step-plan` and `test-spec` start an Improve
child. `--planning-review stage` starts one after each of the five, as before.
`--planning-review none` starts none. The Improve children after
`system-test-author` and `release-plan` and the last `carry-forward` start in
every mode; the quality and test loops and the Backchain child are not covered
and their rules stand. The option's default is a separate owner decision: until
a later dated SPEC commit states it, the code default is `stage`. Every Improve
child that starts is unchanged (a contract the script writes, the same
two-review or unchanged-first-pass exit, no iteration cap), so S-10 holds for
each loop that runs. In `none` a planning result is accepted without a review
loop. What stands in for the loop is what S-9 can name: ShipLoop's gates at
`complete` (cited files exist; the plan's assumption list; the step plan's
commands, criteria, paths and dependency order; the knowledge home's required
files, credential screen and requirement-ID retention); the structural,
record-only `backchain-check`; at `test-author`, a run of the focused commands
that must run a test (a counted test and every listed ID shown on exit 0, a
failing test on a non-zero exit), so a test that cannot load is refused where it
can be fixed; and then the `test-red`, `test-green`, `regression` and
system-test gates, which ShipLoop runs and records. No script-run check at
planning, in any mode, covers whether the spec's criteria are complete and
verifiable, whether the test strategy maps every criterion to a check, or
whether a test spec's oracles are independent. Under `none` those rest on the
producer's own confirmation of the Done-when conditions the packet prints (a
model judgement, printed in every mode), on the later gates and on the
end-of-work review. An Improve child's own S-9 evidence has been loop mechanics
the script counts (passes, the review streak, a Git cross-check, the commit
rule), never a check of the review's content, so `none` removes a second look,
not a script-run check. In `none` the plan child's stopped-child reconciliation
(`improve-reconcile`) and the plan-time experiments it hosts do not exist (the
plan's assumption list is still checked at `complete`); the spec and test
strategy are committed to the knowledge home before any review; and the first
Improve child of a run, and so the first loading of the Improve card, is the
last item's `carry-forward`. Basis: in the Luna xhigh run the planning window
was 375.9 minutes, 203.4 (54%) in five Improve children (22 passes), and in the
Grok medium run 72.7 minutes, 42.4 (58%) in five children (26 passes); the Luna
reviews made five warranted fixes and did not raise the `test-red` defect whose
redo cost 165.9 minutes; a Sonnet 5.5 battleship run's plan review did raise the
same class (a plan with no importable server seam, commit b1e196d), and in a
condensed-packet experiment the planning review with the platform-claim bullet
caught 10 of 15 real plan-stage platform errors against 0 of 15 without it
(Sonnet, three trials per cell). No run without the planning reviews exists, so
the rate of defects that escape without them is unknown. Record:
docs/shiploop-planning-review-plan-2026-10-05.md.

The commit also marks as superseded, with the date 2026-10-05 and the reason: plan item c6 and decision D4 in docs/shiploop-fast-planning-plan-2026-10-04.md ('revisit as its own option'; this is that option), the invariant 'Every planning result gets its own Improve child' in docs/shiploop-delivery-overhead-plan-2026-09-23.md, and, in the new plan doc, the sentence 'Improve's planning-stage passes stay' of commit 9747d769 (a commit message is not edited). It carries the decision record (modes, what each keeps and loses, the carrier of each exit criterion per stage and mode, the Change-admission dispositions for both attacks' findings and the owner's rules, alternatives considered with the reason each is out of scope: the ledger's L1 replacement review, L2 single pass, L3 one review at the end, L7 lazy planning, and a plan-only value), the evidence directory docs/experiments/shiploop-planning-review-20261005/ (the final design, the investigation reports and attacks as text, the Sonnet commit b1e196d message and the E6b excerpt, the probe-judge and per-pass scripts with their output), the LEARNINGS entry 'Planning review', the changed SPEC pins in test/shiploop-e2e.test.py, and 'No-Change-Note: docs and harness tests only; no skills/ or agents/ path changes.' The value-parity test (carve-out values equal PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES) arrives with I1 as a subset check and with I2 as equality; the default parity test arrives with I5b, because the SPEC states no default until I5a. If the owner chooses once (D2), a second SPEC commit before I4 adds the `--planning-review once` clause and its behaviour; if the owner chooses a different default, the I5a sentence changes, not this text.

quality_risk: What the review bought (labels are judgement, no ground truth). Luna xhigh: 22 passes gave 5 warranted fixes, 5 minor, 2 corrections and 10 no change [ledger F10, interim]; the five were traceability, a fixture bypass of the real rules module, untested /api/new recovery, JSON content-type oracles and a W3 ready-check. Grok medium: 26 passes, 4 that fixed a real defect, 6 marginal, 4 churn, 12 no change [I, one investigation]; its spec review took 9 passes, four consecutive commits widening one import allow-list [M]. 1.16.1 max: first passes found warranted defects in 6 of 9 children and 13 of 32 later passes changed something (3 warranted, 7 marginal, 3 churn) [I, one report, docs/shiploop-fast-planning-plan-2026-10-04.md c6]. Measured catches the draft omitted (accepted finding A1-3): (1) a Sonnet 5.5 battleship run, skill-craft 1.16.0, commit b1e196d 'Plan: add server entry guard so tests import without listening': 'Review: plan lacked an importable server design; tests needing a port would be flaky' [M, git -C /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs/20261003/batch-sonnet/battleship/work show b1e196d], the same no-loadable-seam class that cost Luna 165.9 min when its reviews missed it; the planning commits of that run span about 3.6 min, so none would save about 2 min there (13 passes in 125 s [M, ledger]) and lose this catch; (2) E6b: the planning review with the platform-claim bullet caught 10 of 15 real plan-stage platform errors against 0 of 15 without it [M, docs/shiploop-composition-state-experiments-2026-09-26.md; limits: Sonnet, condensed packets, 3 trials per cell, the judge shares gaps]; under none that review does not run. Under once the plan child keeps both, but after test-strategy and plan were written against an unreviewed spec (cascade cost unmeasured; covered accepted records stay stale). No script check at planning covers these classes (weak or missing oracles, traceability, contradictions between documents, an untested stated requirement, a regression command naming criteria it cannot confirm). none also gives up plan reconcile and plan-time experiments, commits an unreviewed spec into the knowledge later runs inherit, and moves the first Improve card resolution to the end of the run. The review missed the costliest defect: on Luna xhigh a plan that gave the tests no real module to load cost a 165.9-minute redo against 99.2 the first time through those stages; the 123-minute 1.16.1 case is an analogue (an implement revise), not the same defect [M, ledger F9]; so one same-class event, with review on, and one catch of the same class on a different host. Break-even: none saves at most 203.4 min on Luna xhigh against an escape costing 66.7 (extra over first pass) to 165.9: 1.2 to 3.0 extra escapes per run [I arithmetic]; on Grok medium none saves at most 42.4 and the cost of an escape was never measured (the probe stopped before test-red): unknown. The escape rate with review off is unknown: no run without planning reviews exists. The default is one constant for every host, so none removes a small, measured catch from fast hosts for about 2 minutes saved (D1). What carries the exit criterion instead, stated honestly. S-9 holds only structurally: the mechanical parts are script-run gates at complete (cited files exist, assumption list, step-plan commands, criteria, paths and order, knowledge-home files, credential screen, requirement-ID retention), the new test-author probe (it carries test-author's own done-when 'each case has a test the focused command runs', which nothing checked before), and the later test-red, test-green, regression and system-test runs. The producer's own confirmation of the Done-when conditions is printed in every mode today: under none it is the same model judgement it always was, not a new check, so it carries nothing the review did not. The semantic parts (complete and verifiable spec criteria, test-strategy mapping, independent oracles) have no script-run check in any mode; this is where the owner's primary rule 'steps iterate until a stated check confirms each exit criterion' and 'enterprise rigour is standard' strain, and the carve-out says so. A script-run requirement-ID presence check was considered and not recommended: the one traceability finding identifiable was a wrong link, which an ID-presence check does not catch, and with no ID in the spec it would pass having run nothing (S-9) [I; I could not read what the Luna finding was]. Considered and out of scope (R-items in the plan doc): ledger L1's replacement review after the first RED or at the end (owner decision D9), L2 single pass (an engine change to required_trivial_reviews, the import validator and an S-10 amendment; on Grok its pass-1 cost leaves the window above 30 [I]), L3 one review at the end, L7 lazy planning (relabels time), a plan-only value (D2).
measurement: Quality first, then tokens, then time (the owner's eval priority); unmeasured is unknown. Baselines: the two 1.21.0 battleship runs, n=1 each, stage times varying about 2x between runs of one model [M stage-clock.md]; they ran 1.21.0, not the tree under test, so the control for any comparison is a stage run of the same checkout. owner_decisions: D1 Default value and gate. Recommended: the code default stays stage until M1 and M2 are read; then flip to none, the only value whose arithmetic reaches the ceiling on Grok medium (26.8 to 30.3 of 72.7, possibly up to about 44 if first-pass work moves into authoring) and which does not reach it on Luna xhigh (172.5 of 375.9 at best). The flip is its own dated SPEC commit plus one constant. Cost named: Sonnet-class hosts lose a measured catch (b1e196d) for about 2 minutes saved. If that matters, keep stage as the default and pass none by the case prompt for slow hosts (no host-sensitive default in the engine: a new surface).

D2 Review-preserving value. Options: once (I4, large, your candidate; at least 36.5 of Grok's 72.7 minutes even if the merged review were free, so it cannot meet 30 on your window), plan (not specified here: children at plan, step-plan and test-spec only, a one-line schedule with no new machinery; Grok 42.6 to 44.4 on the wide window, 27.7 to 29.5 on the narrow one, Luna 270; spec and test-strategy get no review of their own; the plan child's existing cancel-to-reconcile route covers an invalidated upstream premise), or neither. Recommended: neither until M2 shows warranted fixes in none's documents; if one is wanted, plan is the cheaper cut. Choosing once adds a SPEC commit and I4 before the flip.

D3 Accept the carve-out text: it relaxes S-9, S-10 and the primary rule 'steps iterate until a stated check confirms each exit criterion' for five planning stages, names that no script-run check covers semantic planning criteria in any mode, names the loss of plan reconcile and plan-time experiments under none, and names that the first Improve card resolution moves to the end of the run.

D4 Reject the candidate's per-item merge (step-plan and test-spec reviewed once after test-spec). Recommended: yes. A child bound to test-spec cannot amend the step plan's steps, test_commands, criteria or paths, so a structural fix becomes a revise and a re-authoring pass (the Luna redo's step-plan took 120.1 min against 38.7), and it would save only the test-spec child (2.5 to 3.0 min on Grok, 14.2 on Luna).

D5 Land the test-author probe (I3) first, before the option. Recommended: yes. It is the only cheap script-run guard for the plan-gives-the-tests-no-module defect and under none nothing else would look at it before test-red. It lets test-author create the smallest loadable placeholder named in the step plan's paths (no script enforces what test-author edits [M]), a small stage-semantics decision; the first version of the probe accepted runs that ran nothing and is corrected here.

D6 Does the 30-minute ceiling count per-item W1 planning (select-work, step-plan, test-spec: 96.0 min of Luna's 375.9, 14.4 of Grok's 72.7) and a W1 revise redo? The journal defines the window as intake to the first test-spec accept [M], which includes per-item planning and excludes the redo; ledger lever L7 counts differently.

D7 E2E channel: none is needed for control and treatment (--source checkout). Optional: record planning_review in baseline rows and in the Run Review export so cells are not compared across modes silently (a handoff to the Run Review session).

D8 Release timing. The new state key refuses every saved 1.21.x run, including both 1.21.0 battleship run directories if anyone resumes them; no E2E process was running when I looked. Tell the E2E session before releasing.

guard_for_the_missing_module: Yes: increment I3, the test-author probe, independent of the option, landing first and required before the default flips. Why the existing gate did not help [M]: _test_red_gate returns immediately unless the submitted outcome is done, and the Luna host sent revise at test-red ('the focused command was not run because it would fail during import; test-red forbids product-code edits'); nothing owned the missing module (test-red says 'Do not edit product code'; its not-red refusal says 'fix the test setup' with no owner for a loadable seam); test-author's own done-when ('each case in the test spec has a test the focused command runs') had no script check because the row has no complete_runs. The guard: on done at test-author, ShipLoop runs the item's focused commands once through the existing test_loop.verify path in probe mode and accepts only when a test ran: exit 0 is judged in passing mode (a counted test, at least min_tests, every listed ID shown) and a non-zero exit in red mode (a failing test inside a test); accepted statuses are passed and red; refused are no-tests, too-few-tests, ids-missing, uncounted and not-red, with a header and closing sentence of its own that name the placeholder rule. The first version of this design judged everything in red mode and accepted 'green'; I reproduced on seven recorded outputs that this accepts an exit-0 run with no readable count and an exit-0 run whose listed IDs never appear, while the corrected judge refuses both and still accepts a counted pass, a counted red and refuses the Node missing-module output (ids-missing with IDs, uncounted without) and 'Ran 0 tests' [M, probe_judge.py]. After MAX_REFUSED_RUNS refused runs done is refused and revise is the named remedy (_remedy('test-author') is revise because _finish adds revise to every INNER row from test-spec on [M]); the gate returns for any outcome but done, so the host can always revise. The refusal comes at test-author, where creating the smallest loadable placeholder named in the step plan's paths is allowed: edits={'tests'} is descriptive only and scope_refusal at implement applies to no-test items only [M]. Two generic sentences go into the test-author and step-plan duties (S-8). Cost: one focused-command run at test-author's done, seconds, the same path ShipLoop already runs at test-red [I]. Saving if it had existed: up to the 165.9-minute redo on Luna xhigh less a few minutes [I]; it protects the run total, not the planning window. Not covered: a test that contradicts its own helper (the 1.16.1 implement revise) looks RED at test-red. Rejected alternatives: static import analysis (language-specific, S-8), a Backchain consumer (the graph models implement steps only), lint (needs a configured resolver), text alone (the Luna reviews and host ignored text of this kind), gating revise at test-red on a ShipLoop run (the host can still only revise, the costly route). Lives in: shiploop_stage_spec.py, shiploop_test_loop.py, shiploop_navigator.py, shiploop_prompts.py; tests in test/shiploop-test-loop.test.py, test/shiploop-stage-spec.test.py and test/shiploop-navigator-contract.test.py.
